subject: physics
title: Nuclear Binding Energy and E = mc²
welcome_lead: Weigh a nucleus, find the mass defect and unlock binding energy with E = mc².
meta_desc: A-Level Nuclear adventure on mass defect, binding energy and E=mc².
final_note: Iron-56 sits at the binding-energy peak — that is why stars stop fusing there.

concepts.def: Energy released equals lost mass × c².
Energy to separate nucleus into nucleons.

walkthroughs.body_html: A nucleus has slightly less mass than the sum of its protons and neutrons. The missing mass Δm has been converted to binding energy that holds nucleons together.
Multiply mass defect (kg) by c² (≈ 9 × 10¹⁶ m²/s²) to get binding energy in joules. Often quoted in MeV using 1 u ≈ 931.5 MeV/c².
BE per nucleon peaks near iron-56 at ~8.8 MeV. Fission of heavy nuclei (uranium) and fusion of light nuclei (hydrogen) both move towards iron, releasing energy.
